course_summary:
ISEN 617 | Quantitative Models for Supply Chain Coordination | Spring 2026
Instructor: Joseph Geunes | geunes@tamu.edu
Meets: TR 12:45PM - 2:00PM | ZACH 266
Grading: Homework Assignments [20%], Four Quizzes [80%] — A: 90-100, B: 80-89, C: 70-79, D: 60-69, F: <60
Topics: The Traveling Salesman Problem, The Vehicle Routing Problem, Economic Order Quantity, Power-of-Two Policies, Economic Production Quantity, Guaranteed Service Models, The Bullwhip Effect, channel coordination models, vendor-managed inventory models, Multiechelon Inventory Models, Series Systems with Stochastic Demand, Multistage EOQ Type Models, Periodic Review with Zero Fixed Costs, Periodic Review with Nonzero Fixed Costs, Continuous Review, Dynamic, Deterministic Demand, Classical Methods, Forecast Accuracy, Quantity Discounts, Backorders, Pooling, Flexibility, Facility Location Models, Supply Uncertainty, Integrated Supply Chain Models, supply chain contracting, model operations processes, inventory costs, transportation costs, multistage systems, operations tradeoffs, conflicting incentives, coordinate operations, Forecasting, Demand Modeling, Deterministic Inventory Models, Stochastic Inventory Models, supply chain management, inventory, models, concepts, complexities
Tools: ProQuest Ebook Central
